note: The per-family closure surface for Q11 (`no-input`, catalogue category `nonExistentInput`) at GOAL_SPEC.md 9.1. It publishes the outputs 1 to 10 status list for this one family, with the exact evidence behind each applicable output and an explicit justification for anything not applicable. Every count in this artifact was measured from a runner report produced by demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q11.mjs in this tree: one batched `aiken check -e` invocation under the pinned fork compiler for the on-chain selectors, and one Vitest run per cited suite. Nothing is counted from test source, from prose, or from a sibling artifact's numbers. LOCAL_PASS is the only passing status this artifact may record; the live half of a family's closure is owned exclusively by the Q57 sweep and QG3 and is never recorded in a family-local artifact. Outputs 5 to 8 are bound family-locally in the SHARED four-family artifact docs/exec-plans/evidence/canonical-v1-proof-family-q1x-v1.json, whose own gate demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q1x.mjs is the executable authority for those cells and runs in the same battery; this artifact records the delegation explicitly, re-reads the shared artifact's Q11 cells, and re-checks that the concrete Q11 surfaces those cells describe exist and are wired, rather than re-running the shared suites a second time. Output 10 is OPEN: the two parent-owned matrices are measured below and neither records this family's local status yet. One structural difference from the Q10 twin is measured rather than inherited: this family's emulator lifecycle lives in a suite it SHARES with two sibling ledger-rule families, so the lifecycle marker scan is scoped to this family's own `it` block instead of the whole file, and the count of lifecycles the suite executes is published separately from the count this family owns.

compiler.rationale: .github/workflows/aiken-ci.yml pins exactly one compiler for compilation, for every applied validator hash and for executing the test suite: the patched fork built from Anastasia-Labs/aiken rev 2a78108ccb184161689b8a06c84d942e13b5b209 (tag midgard-2a78108c), whose AIKEN_FORK_VERSION is `aiken v1.1.23+2a78108`. Stock v1.1.22 was retired from every role because the build that used to hold the compilation role ships a live unsound-codegen defect. The identity is therefore measured by spawning the resolved binary and is required to match the pin EXACTLY, not by prefix: a second fork build of the same 1.1.23 base reports a different `+<rev>` suffix and would supply this family's on-chain result under a compiler the tree does not pin.

output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.rule: A block is invalid if a transaction committed by its `transactions_root` spends an input that never existed at that point of the ledger: the spent out-ref is absent from the block's `prev_utxos_root` AND its producing transaction is absent from the same block's counted `transactions_root`. Two absence claims against two authenticated roots are the decisive pair; the on-chain family proves exactly that, one claim per step in step-03 and step-04.

localEnforcement.note: Both sites are the same rule on the two candidate-application paths: a spent out-ref that resolves to nothing in the ledger state in view is rejected with the phantom out-ref as its detail. The identifier is additionally carried at two further, deliberately uncounted sites in the same file — a `reject(...)` for a missing REFERENCE input and a structured `{ kind: "rejected", code: ... }` return on the resolve-inputs path — so the count is scoped to the `fail(...)` spend-input rule this family corrects rather than to every mention of the code.

catalogueBinding.note: The append-only id is the positional index encoded big-endian over FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_ID_BYTE_COUNT bytes, so index 1 is the 8-hex-digit id 00000001. The index is re-derived from the order constant rather than trusted, because inserting a category rather than appending one would silently re-number every family after it — and this family sits at index 1, immediately behind `doubleSpend`, so it is the first family such an insertion would move.

registeredFamiliesSuiteNotCited.reason: The registered-families lifecycle suite carries three lifecycles — no-reference-input, reference-input-no-idx and invalid-signature — and no no-input lifecycle at all. It is therefore deliberately NOT cited for this family, and the absence is measured rather than assumed: the verifier requires the suite source to contain no `nonExistentInput` occurrence, so a future no-input lifecycle added there fails this gate until it is cited. Q11's catalogue-reachability passage is carried instead by the output-9 emulator journey, which asserts the computation-thread asset name against the deployed catalogue's `nonExistentInput` category id.

output3FlatFieldHashBinding.boundFieldNote: Field 0 is the field this family opens, and it opens it exactly once. Step-02 authenticates the carried spend-inputs preimage against the field-0 commitment of the transaction step-01 bound — authenticate-once against the positionally-extracted `field_hash_0` of the committed compact structure the thread's `bad_tx_id` anchors, never against a free-standing hash argument (spec section 4's positional-identity invariant, section 7 item 1). The thread deliberately carries the transaction's ID rather than a field commitment, so the door is re-opened from the anchor at the one step that needs it. The out-of-range selector in step-02 is section 7 item 3, abort-never-clamp: a clamped read would hand the family a real committed input while the prover named an index the transaction never had. Steps 03 and 04 open no field: they carry non-membership claims against the two block roots step-01 authenticated.

output4OnchainSelectors.claim: Every deployed step of the family carries at least one positive selector and at least one valid-block negative selector, and all of them are measured passing in one batched run under the pinned fork compiler.
output4OnchainSelectors.selectionNote: `aiken check -m <module>.{<test>}` names exactly one test, so the batch is exact: the run must collect precisely the declared selectors and no others. `aiken check` exits 0 on a selector that matches nothing, so a zero-collection or partial-collection run has to be failed by the derivation rather than by the exit code. The declared set is additionally cross-checked against every `test` declaration the four modules contain, so a selector added to one of these modules and left uncited fails this gate — which is how the two witness-faithful step-03 exclusion arms landed by #582 are held in the census rather than absorbed into the single selector they replaced.

selectors.claim: The challenged transaction is genuinely committed under the block's counted `transactions_root`, so its verified id, the header's `prev_utxos_root` and the authenticated raw transactions root all reach step-02.

The same binding through a 22-level membership proof carried by published chunks — the carriage route added at issue #545, past the direct route's envelope ceiling — with the authenticated root still reaching step-02 for the later absence checks.
Published chunks stay bound to the header's counted transactions root; a forged root cannot bind.
The step is bound to the exact claim its redeemer named, so a merkelized verifier invoked on a different chunk order proves nothing this step asked for.

A transaction fabricated against a VALID block's header cannot bind: the raw transactions root is not the one that header's counted `transactions_root` commits, so the challenge dies before any non-existence claim is made.
The carried preimage is the one the disputed transaction's field-0 commitment authenticates, so the input at the challenged index is carried to step-03 together with both block roots.

A valid block commits each transaction's real spend-inputs collection, so the only way to name an input the transaction never spent is to carry a different preimage; the door's authenticate-once hash check rejects it.
Spec section 7 item 3, abort-never-clamp, at the family's own call site: an index past the committed collection fails the read instead of returning the nearest item.

The genesis arm (#582): a first block over a genesis confirmed state carries `env.empty_merkle_tree_root` as `prev_utxos_root`, and the empty proof is the only — and a genuine — absence witness an empty ledger can produce, bound to the canonical `MidgardTxInput` CBOR key of the forwarded input.

The populated arm (#582): the same delegated claim against a non-empty root, carrying the real single-leaf absence witness that reconstructs it — the arm every block after the first takes, and the one an empty-proof-only selector could never have exercised.

In a valid block the spent input really is in the initial ledger, so the only non-membership claim a prover can obtain is for some other key; binding the claim to a key that is not the forwarded input's canonical CBOR is rejected.
The very same absence claim with the witness living in a referenced publication UTxO and only its index reaching the step redeemer.
The step is bound to the exact claim its redeemer named: a verifier invoked on a different chunk order proves something this step did not ask for.
A published-chunk step that never invokes the merkelized verifier proves nothing at all, so the absent invocation is failed rather than treated as a vacuous success.

The producing transaction of the challenged input is excluded from the block's authenticated raw transactions root — with the carried witness being the block's real committed leaf, and the divergence at the first nibble asserted — so the non-existence proof finalizes into a permanent fraud-proof token.

The non-membership claim must be made against the exact transactions root threaded forward from the authenticated header: a `pexcludes` claim against an unrelated root — the only root under which a genuinely committed producing transaction can look absent — cannot finalize.
The same absence claim finalizes with the witness in a referenced publication UTxO.
The step is bound to the exact claim its redeemer named, on the absence terminal as on the membership one.

delegatedOutputs.rationale: Outputs 5 to 8 are not unowned and are not re-derived here. They are bound family-locally for Q11 inside the SHARED four-family artifact, whose own gate is the executable authority for those cells and runs in the same battery as this one. That gate spawns five Vitest suites, including three emulator suites that drive the complete correction path at forced branch level 22 and at the admissible 296-input Cardano spend shape. Re-running them from this gate would double the battery's cost and would measure nothing the shared gate does not already measure. So this gate delegates the passage and asserts the delegation instead: it re-reads the shared artifact's Q11 cells for outputs 5 to 9, requires each to be LOCAL_PASS with no open cell left anywhere in that artifact, requires Q11 to appear in BOTH carriage remediations' measured-family lists, requires the tier-routed remediation to name this family's binding stage as `step-02`, and then re-checks in this tree that the concrete Q11 surfaces those cells describe still exist and are still wired.
delegatedOutputs.output9Note: The shared artifact also binds output 9 for Q11, and that cell is asserted here as part of the delegation check. Output 9 is nevertheless re-measured locally below by running the emulator suite directly, so this artifact's output-9 row rests on a runner report of its own rather than on a citation.
delegatedOutputs.bindingStageNote: `spendInputTierRoutedCarriage.bindingStages.Q11` is required to be `step-02`, which is this family's own field-0 door and the step the spend-input cardinality axis reaches. Asserting the stage, not only the membership, is what keeps a remediation measured on some other step of the chain from settling the axis for this family.

output6.note: The deployed first-step identity is the applied script the first blueprint title compiles to: `buildNonExistentInputChain` applies parameters to all four titles, and the emulator journey then reaches that first step through the catalogue — its `fraudCategoryName` is asserted to be `nonExistentInput`, its computation-thread asset name to be the deployed `nonExistentInput` category id concatenated with the fraudulent header hash, and the thread UTxO is found at the init result's first-step address. Blueprint regeneration is parent-only (IG1), so the applied hashes themselves are not pinned in this artifact; the titles and the catalogue-derived reachability are.

output7.note: The DA-first builder exists, is exported, and its own body routes through the shared admission gate before it emits any proof material. Its passage is measured by the canonical-evidence suite that output 2 already runs in this gate, so no extra suite is spawned for it.

output8.note: The chain is one prepare verb, one init verb and one submit verb per step, all present in bin.ts's command allowlist. Resumability carries no hidden process state: every non-terminal step module returns `nextThreadOutRef`, so the next step is addressable from the previous submission's result alone, and the terminal module deliberately returns no `nextThreadOutRef` — it returns the permanent `fraudProofUnit` instead. The allowlist itself is section 5.1 serialization-sensitive and parent-integrated, so this artifact reads it and does not propose changes to it.
